The American System. Henry Clay championed this economic policy in the early nineteenth century, combining protective tariffs with federal investment in infrastructure and a national bank. Designed to make the United States independent from British manufacturing, it sparked fierce opposition in the agrarian South, which feared expensive domestic goods and tariffs that hurt their cotton trade. The tariffs led to the Nullification Crisis when South Carolina challenged federal authority. The system became the platform of the Whig Party and later influenced Lincoln's Republicans.
